title: Senior's toolkit: brokers and queues
summary: The Kafka and RabbitMQ commands you use to see lag, read messages, find stuck queues and replay events.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: brokers and queues
body: When messages are late, lost or duplicated, these commands show what the broker actually holds. The Kafka tools ship in the Kafka `bin/` folder as `kafka-*.sh`; some images (Confluent) drop the `.sh`.

toolkit.what: Shows, per partition, the group's committed offset, the latest offset and the LAG between them. Growing lag means consumers are too slow or stuck.
flags: offsets and lag for one group
with `--describe`: which consumer owns which partitions
toolkit.when: the first command when events are "late"

toolkit.what: Moves a group's position, to replay events after a bug fix or to skip past a poison message. The group must have no running consumers.
flags: go back to a point in time
move by a number of messages
show the new offsets only (the default)

toolkit.what: Reads messages from a topic so you can see what producers really sent, including the key that decides the partition.
flags: start at the oldest retained message
print each key next to its value

toolkit.what: Lists a topic's partitions, their leaders, replicas and in-sync replicas. Fewer partitions than consumers means some consumers sit idle.
flags: partitions and replicas of one topic

toolkit.what: Shows each RabbitMQ queue with the columns you ask for. Ready messages with zero consumers is the classic stuck queue.
toolkit.example: rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers
toolkit.when: a queue keeps growing, or a DLQ is filling

toolkit.what: Health checks for a RabbitMQ node: is it up, are alarms raised (memory, disk) that block publishers.
flags: list memory or disk alarms; publishers block while one is set

steps.prompt: Match each command to the question it answers.
pairs: How many partitions does the topic have?
Which queue has messages and nobody reading?

prompt: Invoices are an hour late. `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group billing` shows:
TOPIC   PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG    CONSUMER-ID
What is the most likely cause?
options: The consumer on partition 1 is stuck, often on one message it keeps failing on
The broker is out of disk
steps.explain: Only partition 1 lags; the others keep up. One partition stuck while others flow usually means one consumer is blocked, retrying a poison message or hung on a slow call. Check `billing-2`'s logs, and the message at offset 51002.

steps.prompt: Preview replaying billing from 09:00 yesterday, without changing anything yet.
steps.explain: `--reset-offsets --to-datetime` picks the new position. `--dry-run` prints the offsets it would set; run again with `--execute` once the billing consumers are stopped and the consumer is idempotent, because every event since 09:00 will be processed again.

steps.prompt: `rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers` shows `pick-orders 0 500 1`. Nothing new reaches the warehouse. What does that tell you?
options: The one consumer took 500 messages and is not acknowledging them; it is hung or never acks
The queue is empty, so the producer is broken
steps.explain: Unacknowledged messages are delivered but not finished. With a prefetch of 500 a stuck consumer holds them all and nothing else can get them. Restarting it returns them to the queue; the fix is in the consumer (ack after processing, a lower prefetch, a timeout on the slow call).

steps.prompt: Put a safe replay of Kafka events in order.
lines: Check the consumer handles duplicates (idempotent by event id)
Stop every consumer in the group
Start the consumers and watch the lag fall with `--describe`

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When someone says "the event never arrived", look at the broker before the code: lag per partition in Kafka, ready versus unacked in RabbitMQ. Always `--dry-run` an offset reset first, and only replay into consumers that are idempotent.
